purpose: Explain why an identified official authority or route applies to a property issue, what legal or administrative function supports the route, what the route can and cannot do, and what evidence it requires.
core_principle: ROUTE → FUNCTION → AUTHORITY → LEGAL BASIS → SCOPE → EVIDENCE → LIMITS
rules: Explain the route from its actual legal or administrative function, not from convenience.
Distinguish authority to hold/provide a record from authority to decide a dispute.
Distinguish registration authority from substantive adjudication unless the governing source provides otherwise.
Identify the exact source supporting the route where material.
State the limits of the route so citizens do not expect an authority to provide a remedy outside its function.
Required evidence is tied to the requested function and proposition.
Alternative routes are shown only where supported by an authoritative source.
Review, appeal, complaint and court routes remain distinct.
Deadlines are shown only when governing source, trigger and counting rule are verified.
The explanation describes the route; it does not guarantee an outcome.
hard_stops: Never invent legal authority for a route.
Never treat a service webpage as proof of substantive legal power without the relevant source.
Never imply a record custodian can determine a dispute without authority.
Never imply an application guarantees the requested result.
Never invent evidence requirements, fees, forms or deadlines.
Never expose restricted evidence or internal reasoning.
